acc.heading: Website Blocking Check
acc.subtitle: Check whether Cloudflare Radar top sites are blocked by HDSB on your current network
acc.body: The web version is limited by browser CORS, so results may be unreliable. Download the standalone blocking-check app for more accurate and complete results.
acc.download: Download the blocking checker on GitHub
acc.macTitle: macOS says the app is damaged
acc.macBody: Apps downloaded from GitHub are not signed by Apple, so macOS may say it "is damaged and can't be opened". The file is fine — run this in Terminal to remove the restriction (replace the path with the actual app):
acc.macNote: Alternatively, open System Settings → Privacy & Security, find the blocked notice at the bottom and click "Open Anyway".
acc.platform:
The app supports Android, Windows, macOS and Linux.
Why not iOS? Because I can't afford an App Store certificate.
So Apple users who want to run a check can now open your computer, or borrow a nearby Android friend's phone.
acc.about: HDSB intercepts and tampers with access to some websites at the network edge. The checker visits the sites in the Cloudflare Radar Top list one by one to determine whether they are blocked, so you can see what is reachable on your current network.
acc.feature1: Batch-checks the reachability of Cloudflare Radar Top sites
acc.feature2: Classifies results as reachable / blocked / unreachable / timeout and counts them
acc.feature3: Shows per-domain details and exports the results as CSV
acc.how: When a request is blocked by HDSB, it usually returns an interception page, or replaces the site certificate with one issued by the interception device. The checker uses this to decide whether a site is blocked.
acc.tip1: Run it on an HDSB network, otherwise the results are meaningless
acc.tip2: Results may vary with time and network, for reference only
acc.tip3: It queries many domains, so the first run may take a while

about.heading: About EFH
about.subtitle: Clarify: i have absolute no willing to write this blyat about page so the content below is fully uncensored ai generated and i dont wanna care.
about.intro: EFH (Escape From HDSB Project) is a network acceleration and internet-freedom project slowly built in spare time by a group of students chased by homework and firewalls alike. We believe the internet should have no borders.
about.mission: We run four nodes across different regions to provide stable, low-latency proxy access, alongside small tools such as one-click config import, service status and a standalone blocking-check app — so everyone can climb over the wall named HDSB.
about.stack: The server is Kotlin + Ktor; nodes run trojan-go with nginx, and certificates renew automatically via acme.sh. The frontend is plain HTML / CSS / JavaScript, proudly zero-dependency and fast to load.
about.disclaimer: This project is for learning and researching network technology only. Please follow the laws of your region. Any consequence of using this service is borne by the user.
